hook_text: Twelve pieces of paper land on your desk. Three books. Can you put every one in the right place first time?
clip_script: August at Ridgeview Hardware. Twelve documents. Three questions. Did money come in? Cash sales, rent, customers paying: the cash receipts journal. Did money go out? Wages, stock paid by EFT, the owner's withdrawal, bank charges: the cash payments journal. Did goods leave on a promise? The debtors journal. Five, four, three. Now add up. Money in: 22 600. Check it: sales 10 500, debtors 9 600, rent 2 500. Matches. Money out: 9 450. Stock, wages, other. Matches. Credit sales 7 500. Customers owed 12 500, bought 7 500 more, paid 9 600. They owe 10 400 now, and their pages agree. Sorting first is the whole trick.
visual_style: Documents dropping onto a desk and flying into three labelled books, columns adding up, a cross-cast tick appearing on each.
pacing: Fast sorting montage, then three quick checks, each ending with a tick.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort Ridgeview's August transactions yourself.
